clauses.label: Se c t io n 1.
clauses.text:
Se c t io n 1. The Secretary of Labor shall issue rules and regulations 
requiring each department and agency of the executive branch of the 
Federal Government to list suitable employment openings with the 
appropriate office of the State Employment Service or the United 
States Employment Service. This section shall not be construed as 
requiring the employment of individuals referred by such office or as 
superseding any requirements of the Civil Service Laws. Rules, regula­
tions, and orders to implement this section shall be developed in 
consultation with the Civil Service Commission.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. The Secretary of Labor is hereby designated and empowered 
to exercise, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the 
President, the authority of the President under Section 2012 of Title 38 
of the United States Code.

clauses.label: Sec. 3.
clauses.text:
Sec. 3. The Secretary of Labor shall gather information on the 
effectiveness of the program established under this order and Section 
2012 of Title 38 of the United States Code and of the extent to which 
the employment service system is fulfilling the employment needs of 
veterans. The Secretary of Labor shall, from time to time, report to 
the President concerning his evaluation of the effectiveness of this order 
along with his recommendations for further action which the Secretary 
believes to be appropriate.

clauses.label: Sec. 4.
clauses.text:
Sec. 4. Appropriate departments and agencies shall, in consultation 
with the Secretary of Labor, issue such amendments or additions to
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 38, N O . 18— M O N D AY, JANU ARY 29, 1973

procurement rules and regulations as may be necessary to carry out 
the purposes of this order and Section 2012 of Title 38 of the United 
States Code. Except as otherwise provided by law, all executive depart­
ments and agencies are directed-to cooperate with the Secretary of 
Labor, to furnish the Secretary of Labor with such information and 
assistance as he may require in the performance of his functions under 
this order, and to comply with rules, regulations, and orders of the 
Secretary.

clauses.text:

own_original_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11701
Employment of Veterans by Federal Agencies and Government 
Contractors and Subcontractors
On June 16, 1971, I issued Executive Order No. 11598 to facilitate 
the employment of returning veterans by requiring Federal agencies 
and Federal contractors and their subcontractors to list employment 
openings with the employment service systems. Section 503 of the Viet­
nam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act of 1972 (Public Law 
92-540; 86 Stat. 1097) added a new section 2012 to Title 38 of the 
United States Code which, in effect, provides statutory authority to 
extend the program developed under that order with respect to Govern­
ment contractors and their subcontractors.
NOW , THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 301 of Title 3 of the United States Code and as President of 
the United States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Se c t io n 1. The Secretary of Labor shall issue rules and regulations 
requiring each department and agency of the executive branch of the 
Federal Government to list suitable employment openings with the 
appropriate office of the State Employment Service or the United 
States Employment Service. This section shall not be construed as 
requiring the employment of individuals referred by such office or as 
superseding any requirements of the Civil Service Laws. Rules, regula­
tions, and orders to implement this section shall be developed in 
consultation with the Civil Service Commission.
Sec. 2. The Secretary of Labor is hereby designated and empowered 
to exercise, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the 
President, the authority of the President under Section 2012 of Title 38 
of the United States Code.
Sec. 3. The Secretary of Labor shall gather information on the 
effectiveness of the program established under this order and Section 
2012 of Title 38 of the United States Code and of the extent to which 
the employment service system is fulfilling the employment needs of 
veterans. The Secretary of Labor shall, from time to time, report to 
the President concerning his evaluation of the effectiveness of this order 
along with his recommendations for further action which the Secretary 
believes to be appropriate.
Sec. 4. Appropriate departments and agencies shall, in consultation 
with the Secretary of Labor, issue such amendments or additions to
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 38, N O . 18— M O N D AY, JANU ARY 29, 1973

=== PDF page 8 of 64 ===
2676 THE PRESIDENT
procurement rules and regulations as may be necessary to carry out 
the purposes of this order and Section 2012 of Title 38 of the United 
States Code. Except as otherwise provided by law, all executive depart­
ments and agencies are directed-to cooperate with the Secretary of 
Labor, to furnish the Secretary of Labor with such information and 
assistance as he may require in the performance of his functions under 
this order, and to comply with rules, regulations, and orders of the 
Secretary.
Sec. 5. Executive Order No. 11598 of June 16, 1971, is hereby 
superseded.
T h e W h it e H o u s e,
January 24, 1973.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 11701 (38 FR 2675, signed 1973-01-24) has five sections: (1) the Secretary of Labor shall issue rules requiring each executive department and agency to list suitable employment openings with the State Employment Service or the United States Employment Service, in consultation with the Civil Service Commission; (2) the Secretary of Labor is designated and empowered to exercise, without presidential approval, the President's authority under section 2012 of title 38, United States Code (now 38 U.S.C. 4212); (3) the Secretary of Labor shall gather information on the effectiveness of the program and report to the President from time to time; (4) agencies shall issue procurement rule amendments in consultation with the Secretary and cooperate with and comply with the Secretary's rules; (5) Executive Order No. 11598 of June 16, 1971 is superseded. The dossier inventory omitted section 1, so it is corrected to the five sections of the order. Section 5 supersedes EO 11598 and was carried out when the order issued on 1973-01-24. Sections 1 to 4 have no sunset, condition or own-terms end. The held U.S. Code text of 38 U.S.C. 4212 prints Ex. Ord. versions.research_rationale: EO 11701 (Jan. 24, 1973, 38 FR 2675) implements the veterans employment-listing program: section 1 directs the Secretary of Labor to issue rules requiring executive agencies to list suitable openings with the State or U.S. Employment Service; section 2 delegates the President's authority under former 38 U.S.C. 2012 to the Secretary; section 3 directs information gathering and reporting 'from time to time'; section 4 directs agencies to amend procurement regulations and cooperate; section 5 supersedes EO 11598. The complete held original was read. The dossier inventory was INCOMPLETE: it began at section 2 and omitted section 1, the core command. An inventory correction (five disjoint spans) restores section 1; sections 2-5 are the dossier's own spans. Earlier-end tests: no own-term, sunset, condition or report-deadline term (dossier own_terms empty; section 3 reporting is open-ended, not a deadline); no ACT record, chain event or conflict. D6: searched (1) the dossier chain (empty), (2) both EDGES.csv files (no row targets EO 11701), (3) all 6,652 held fr-originals texts to EO 14435 for citations by number in word and bare-list form: none. In particular EO 12107 (1978), which swapped Civil Service Commission for the Office of Personnel Management across its listed personnel orders, does not list EO 11701, so section 1's 'consultation with the Civil Service Commission' was never textually amended; successor-agency substitution is a legal inference and is flagged here for the reviewer, (4) the machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 to 2026-10-09, which prints the order as a note to 38 U.S.C. 4212 and is a lead only; eCFR to 2026-10-14; OFR catalog 0 hits). basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). Conditions checked: no unresolved ACT record or specific missing line, no own-term end, no conflict, searches reach 2026-10-14 (U.S. Code edition at 2026-10-09 disclosed). Judgment flags for the reviewer: (i) sections 4 and 5 contain a one-time implementing direction and a completed supersession; I treat their continuing legal effect as operative but a reviewer may call this ONE_TIME_COMMAND or PARTIAL_SCOPE; (ii) former 38 U.S.C. 2012 was renumbered 4212 and amended after 1973 (for example 2002), so section 2's delegation is read to follow the renumbered section, which the Code's own note placement supports but no held text states. No human certification is asserted.
